title: histogram-bucketed-batching-adaptive
author: Priya Shah
description:
Motivation: We observed persistent cost due to excessive padding when latency-sensitive traffic mixes short and long sequences. Prior seqlen bucketing used static thresholds and non-adaptive heuristics which either over-fragmented batches or caused large padding waste. This change implements an online, histogram-driven bucketing strategy that adapts bucket boundaries to the observed sequence-length distribution and factors in KV-cache reuse likelihood to prioritize co-batching requests that will benefit from warmed KV state.

Design summary: 1) Runtime keeps a lightweight ring-histogram (per-worker, time-decayed) of recent request sequence lengths. Boundaries are derived by splitting the histogram into N target-quantiles; bucket boundaries are smoothed with exponential moving averages to avoid thrashing. 2) Each bucket tracks average seq_len, sample variance, and an empirical KV-cache hit-rate (based on prefix-key fingerprint reuse). Buckets expose a small metadata struct used by the scheduler to compute an expected padding cost and an expected cache-benefit score. 3) Scheduler scoring: new priority = alpha*(expected_padding_waste) + beta*(1 - kv_cache_hit_rate) + gamma*(latency_headroom_factor), where alpha/beta/gamma are tunable via runtime flags and can be adjusted by policy. Lower score means higher batching priority (i.e., the scheduler will prefer groups that minimize padding and maximize cache reuse). 4) Kernel selection hints: when a bucket's max_len <= threshold we emit a kernel_hint to prefer fast int8 kernels / packed attention kernels; this reduces per-token latency for common short buckets. 5) Continuous-batching integration: the bucketed scheduler respects the existing continuous batching time-window and backlog signals; when backlog is low we allow coarser merging across adjacent buckets up to a padding budget. 6) Safety & rollout: feature gated and guarded by canary config; bucket adaptivity has upper bounds on boundary movement per-minute and exposes metrics for observability.

Behavioural changes vs previous approach: - Replaces static, config-defined cutoffs with live quantile boundaries. - Prioritizes KV-cache friendliness as a first-class factor so that warmed contexts (e.g., multi-turn chat floods) are grouped together even if lengths differ slightly. - Allows controlled cross-bucket packing when backlog/latency signals indicate underutilization.

Benchmarks (internal perf-lab, x1 V100 equivalent, mixed-seq workload sampled from production traces): - End-to-end token cost per-minute: -12.4% median, -9.1% p95 under baseline config. - Throughput (tokens/sec): +18% at 95th percentile while p99 latency stayed within 3% of baseline SLO. - KV-cache hit-rate increased by +7.3 percentage points for multi-turn tests. - Microbench (per-bucket) shows padding waste drop from 21% -> 8% for heavy-tailed traces.

Implementation notes & files: small, focused changes distributed across batching and scheduler subsystems. New unit + integration tests added to exercise boundary adaptation, safety caps, kernel hints, and behaviour under low/high backlog. A canary flag (runtime.feature.hist_bucket_v1) gates the whole path.

Why this is safe to merge: feature-flagged, conservative defaults (N=6 buckets, small smoothing factor), extensive unit tests, and CI e2e runs with synthetic heavy-tail traces. We validated canary runs on a Dedicated pool for 48h with no regressions in p99 errors.

Operational guidance (added to docs/observability): - Metrics: runtime.batching.bucket_boundaries, runtime.batching.bucket_padding_waste, runtime.batching.bucket_kv_hit_rate, runtime.batching.kernel_hint_counts. - Recommended defaults are included but teams operating specialized workloads should tune alpha/beta to prioritize cache vs padding.

Related: builds on prior seqlen-bucketing experiments (see ENG-1101) and is complementary to quantization/kernel-selection work in ENG-1252.
